stemExtracted: Let A = {1,2,3,7} and B = {3,0,–1,7}, which of the following are relation from A to B ?

stepsEnglish: A relation from A to B must consist only of ordered pairs whose first entry belongs to A and second entry belongs to B.
Both pairs have second entry 1, but 1 is not in B.
Therefore R1 is not a relation from A to B.
Check the first and second entries against A and B.
The first entry −1 is not in A and the second entry 1 is not in B.
Therefore R2 is not a relation from A to B.
For each ordered pair, check that the first entry is in A.
The first entries 2, 7 and 1 all belong to A.
The second entries −1, 7 and 3 all belong to B.
Every pair is in A×B, so R3 is a relation from A to B.
A relation from A to B must be a subset of A×B.
The first entry 0 occurs in two pairs, but 0 does not belong to A.
Therefore R4 is not a relation from A to B.
